title: The Launch Agent 7 Artifact may not be edited in any way that violates the Sky Core Atlas, and the Facilitator must enforce this
content:
A.6.1.1.8.2.2.2.2.1.2.1.6 states the limit on the amendment power: "The Launch Agent 7 Artifact cannot be edited in any way that violates the Sky Core Atlas or its specifications of the Sky Primitives, or in any way that is otherwise misaligned. The Operational Facilitator must enforce this rule through their review of Artifact Edit Proposals."

This establishes a hierarchy of norms: the Agent Artifact is subordinate legislation. An Agent-level vote, however large its majority, cannot authorize a change that conflicts with the Atlas or with how the Atlas specifies the Primitives. Agent sovereignty is bounded, not merely guided.

The third clause is the widest: "or in any way that is otherwise misaligned." That extends the restriction past textual conflict to the spirit standard, meaning a proposal fully compatible with the letter of the Atlas can still be rejected. This is the Atlas's spirit-over-letter doctrine landing inside an individual Agent's amendment procedure.

The enforcement clause is the honest part and the weak part. There is no technical mechanism that makes a violating edit impossible — the constraint is discharged entirely through one role's review. The rule's strength therefore equals the Facilitator's diligence and independence, which is exactly why the Facilitator is defined in a separate Executor Agent's Artifact rather than appointed by Launch Agent 7 itself.
description: Agent governance is explicitly subordinate to the Atlas and the Sky Primitives specifications; the constraint is enforced by a human reviewer, not by any technical restriction.
